cav22.coordinateFrame: Original deposited 7MIX Cartesian coordinates; identical frame to targets.json cav22

basis.filter: Centroid of OE1/OE2 atoms of chain A E314, E663, E1365, E1655
basis.gate: Centroid of chain A C-alpha atoms A360, A713, I1417, F1711, the four S6 residues surrounding W768 at the bottom of the hydrophobic gate
basis.axis: Straight line from gate landmark to filter landmark, pointing extracellularly
basis.blockadeStop: Outermost chain B atom projected on the illustrative axis within a 4-Angstrom cylinder, plus 2-Angstrom visual clearance

cav22.mechanism: Ziconotide blocks the extracellular CaV2.2 pore; do not animate it as closing the intracellular gate.
limits: This axis is derived for illustration, not an experimentally measured ion trajectory or a HOLE/MD pore calculation.
7MIX has a closed intracellular gate; removing the displayed toxin does not make this coordinate model an experimentally open channel.
Flow in an unblocked comparison is a functional schematic; ion positions, rate, and stopping point are illustrative.
The PDB z axis is not the membrane normal. Transform these landmarks with exactly the same translation, scale, and rotation as both receptor and ligand.
These landmarks do not establish membrane boundaries or a quantitative pore radius.

sources.supports: Experimental receptor, toxin, and filter-calcium coordinates
Extracellular peptide pore blockade; closed intracellular gate; S6 gate landmarks in Figure 2e
EEEE selectivity-filter residue numbering, independently checked as GLU in 7MIX
